Q5.q: What is the most common reason FHA applications are denied?
Q5.a: Debt-to-income — median 40.3% of cited reasons across the 100 largest lenders

Q6.q: Are small mortgage loans denied more often than large ones?
Q6.a: Yes, in every state measured; the penalty ranges from about 1.3x to 4.45x

Q7.q: How much do FHA denial rates vary between lenders?
Q7.a: 1.8% to 78.7% across the 100 largest — a 44x spread

Q8.q: What share of FHA denials cite "incomplete application"?
Q8.a: Median 1.8% across the 100 largest; highest 75.2% (Carrington Mortgage Services LLC)

Q9.q: Which US metro has the widest spread in FHA denial rates between lenders?
Q9.a: Cleveland, OH — 73.7 points among the five highest-volume lenders in that metro (6.4% to 80.1%). NOTE: this is the widest spread among published high-volume lender sets, not the widest spread among all lenders. Computing across every lender with 100+ decisioned applications produces larger figures in several metros — an independent 2024 computation found 93.71 points in Los Angeles on that basis. Corrected 2026-07-28.
